title: Associated Alcohols & Breweries Ltd - 507526 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q1 FY27 IMFL proprietary volume rose 40% YoY to 0.79 million cases, with revenue up 58% to INR792 million, while consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 11% on ethanol weakness.
summary.overview: Consolidated income from operations was INR2,809 million (+5% YoY), EBITDA INR299 million at 11% margin, and PAT INR178 million (6% margin). The proprietary IMFL brands drove growth, with the CP series volume up 260% YoY and proprietary share of revenue rising to 23% from 17%. Margins compressed mainly from ethanol, where realisations fell on oversupply and lower government quota, and from higher grain prices. Management reiterated about 30% IMFL proprietary volume growth for FY27 and flagged the SDF Kerala bottling plant moving to full operation from April 2027.

financial_highlights.value: INR792 million (INR729 million in opening remarks)

segments.name: IMFL proprietary
segments.commentary: Volume 0.79 million cases (+40% YoY), revenue INR792 million (+58% YoY), realisation INR823 per case (+13%), EBITDA margin 20%. Share of company revenue 23% vs 17% a year earlier. CP series volume rose from 20,300 to 73,000 cases (+260%).

segments.name: ENA
segments.commentary: Volume 7.3 million litres (+35% YoY), revenue INR456 million (+25% YoY). Margin under pressure from lower realisation and higher grain prices. Captive consumption of ENA rose to 59% from 50%.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: Volume +28% YoY but realisations fell on oversupply and lower government quota; sales were partly to private OMCs at about INR52-54 per litre versus about INR64 average from government tender. Segment EBITDA negative; management put breakeven at INR57-60 per litre.

segments.name: IMFL licence / contract manufacturing
segments.commentary: Volume 0.1 million cases and revenue INR132 million, reduced after Inbrew moved from licensing to contract manufacturing; Inbrew business ended mid-Q2 FY26. Licensed volume ballparked at about 1 million cases a year, mainly seasonal Celebration Rum.

segments.name: IMFL (overall, as stated)
segments.commentary: Volume 1.7 million cases, revenue INR734 million, EBITDA margin 18%. IML quota-based business flat as the company is at the top of its annual government quota.

guidance_outlook: IMFL proprietary volume growth of about 30% for FY27, reiterated; management also referred to revenue growth of about 30% YoY for IMFL.
Ethanol: revenue expected flat YoY at maximum capacity; better realisation expected from the OMC annual tender from October 2026; higher quota allocation expected.
SDF Kerala plant: automatic machinery installation underway, operational by December 2026; full-fledged operations from 1 April 2027; target capacity 3.5-4 lakh cases per month.
Tequila (MRP INR5,000-7,000) and premium brandy (Kerala) launches in Q2 FY27; RTD (330 mL can, 8% ABV, 5 flavours, INR120 per can) fully registered in 10-12 states from 1 April 2027.
Malt maturation under way for two single malt variants; revenue expected to show in Q3 FY28 onwards. Target 1-2 brands at 1 million cases in 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: SDF Industries (Kerala distillery-cum-bottling, acquired): upgradation and automation in progress; phased move from 3 job-work units, one unit by December 2026, full shift from April 2027.
Kerala sales about 1.5 lakh cases a month; SDF capacity build-up targeted at 3.5-4 lakh cases a month.
Malt maturation facility operating; in-house malt to support Hillfort blending and two single malt launches.
Ethanol plant kept running on a dedicated basis to qualify for subsidy and interest subvention; not converting to ENA.
demand_pricing: CP series volume 73,000 cases in Q1 FY27 vs 20,300 a year earlier; Central Province is the main growth driver.
Nicobar Gin sells about 500-700 cases a month; Hillfort about 1,000-1,500 cases a month. Maharashtra about 700-900 cases a month, UP slowed on policy change.
Odisha entered in Q1 FY27; Karnataka entry planned this quarter; Chhattisgarh and Delhi growing well.
Hillfort faces world number 1 and 2 competitors; blend revamped with new brand strategy; management expects 1-1.5 years for meaningful results.
Indian tequila market about 1.5 lakh cases a year, of which the target price band is about 40,000 cases; target 10-15% share.

Ethanol: government quota about 30% of annual volume last year; private OMC sales at INR52-54 per litre; raw material grain price average INR21,000 per metric ton, with about INR57-58 per litre total cost.

qa_highlights.question: Would the company shift capacity from ethanol to ENA given ethanol losses?
qa_highlights.answer: No plans to shift; ethanol-only operation continues. Plant is run dedicated to ethanol to qualify for subsidy and interest subvention and to save energy costs.

qa_highlights.question: When will SDF start contributing EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Phased move: one unit to SDF by December 2026, full operations from 1 April 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why did IMFL licensed revenue decline and what is the steady-state base?
qa_highlights.answer: Decline due to Inbrew ending mid-Q2 FY26; Diageo licensing revenue roughly flat. Licensed business ballparked at about 1 million cases a year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did IMFL margin fall from about 22% to 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material prices rose more than 10% QoQ, cutting margin by about 2 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: Is ethanol a separate company candidate given earnings volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: No plans to separate; ethanol is a separately presented vertical and is professionally managed. Focus remains on proprietary brands.

qa_highlights.question: What are the RTD and tequila guidance and market sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: RTD targeted at 3-4% share in entered states; malt about 4%; tequila 10-15% of about 40,000-case target segment. RTD addressable market is 8% ABV segment, expected to grow 15-17%.

risks_watch: Ethanol realisation: margin negative at current prices (about INR52-54 vs INR57-60 breakeven); recovery depends on the October 2026 OMC tender and quota allocation.
Grain price inflation (INR21,000/MT average) squeezing ENA and IMFL margins; monsoon outlook is a key variable.
Execution on SDF plant commissioning (December 2026 start, April 2027 full shift) and the risk of supply disruption during transfer from job-work units.
Hillfort scaling is slow and UP volumes have slowed on a policy change; Maharashtra entry is capital intensive.
Licensed IMFL revenue is now lower after Inbrew moved to contract manufacturing; the IML quota business is capped at the annual tender ceiling.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the proprietary brand story and the pipeline, but noticeably defensive on ethanol and on the falling consolidated margin. Management repeatedly framed ethanol weakness as a cyclical, temporary issue and gave few hard numbers on the pipeline beyond targets.
key_quotes: I am pleased to report our highest ever quarterly IMFL proprietary revenue of INR729 million, registered a robust of 58% year-on-year growth in value and 40% year-on-year growth in volume.

The CP series delivered an impressive 260% year-on-year volume growth in Q1 FY27 with the sales increase from 20,300 cases to 73,000 cases, reflecting strong brand equity and reinforcing its leadership position within the segment.
It's not a one-time quarter thing. but we expect the realization to become better.
The primary objective is to do our own brands. That's the primary first and foremost objective.
